title: Midnight quant anomaly casefile: fp8/int8/bf16 traces
content:
Purpose:
Quick freeform log for the late-night debugging session where model outputs suddenly turned to NaN under fp8/integer-backed kernels. Trying to capture commands, raw snippets, and hypotheses for follow-ups and handoff. Goal: reproduce with minimal surface area and isolate whether this is an FP backend (CUDA/AMX), runtime kernel, or quantization transform bug.

Environment snapshot (container):
- image: redwood/runtime-debug:2024-02-02-nightly
- python 3.11.4, pytorch 2.2.0+cu121, cuda 12.1, cudnn 8.9, nvcc 12.1
- compiler: gcc 11.4; CUDA toolkit nvcc reports sm_80
- runtime build: runtime commit 8b3f2e1 (PR 2876 applied locally)
- GPU: A100-SXM4-40GB (driver 535.xx)

Model / workload:
- model: open-variant-7B (Transformer, rotary embeddings) converted with quant-aware flow to fp8-e4m3 per our new schema
- seq_len: 2048 for repro run; often triggers after ~1500 tokens in long-chunked generation
- batch sizes tested: 1, 2, 4
- kv-cache enabled, dynamic batching disabled for these repro runs

Observed failure mode:
- After ~50-200 tokens, logits contain NaN and generation stalls; sometimes final token becomes NaN not earlier logits
- In other runs, loss starts increasing exponentially (overflow) then NaN
- BF16 and FP32 runs do not show NaN (control runs OK)
- INT8 (symmetric) runs show degraded quality but no NaNs in most cases

Commands tried (repro commands and flags):
- baseline (works):
  python run_inference.py --model open-variant-7B --dtype bf16 --seq 2048 --quant none --seed 42

- failing (fp8):
  CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 python run_inference.py --model open-variant-7B --dtype fp8 --seq 2048 --quant e4m3 --seed 42 2>&1 | tee /tmp/fp8-run.log

- reduced: shorter seq to isolate: seq=512 and seq=1024 (NaNs less frequent at 512)
- kernel toggles: --disable-fused-gemm, --disable-kv-fusion, --use-cublas-gemm
- RNG toggles: --rng-seed 0 --rng-seed 1 --rng-seed 42 --rng-seed 99999
- denorm toggles: export CUDA_FLUSH_DENORMS_TO_ZERO=1 (also tried OFF)

Partial error snippet captured (fp8 run with CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1):
Timestamp 2024-03-12T02:14:43Z
...
RuntimeError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered (external/runtime/ops/gemm_kernels.cu:438)
  File "/opt/venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/torch/nn/modules/module.py", line 1190, in _call_impl
    return forward_call(*input, **kwargs)
  File "run_inference.py", line 322, in forward
    logits = self.head(x)
...
Stack (user frame): runtime/ops/gemm_kernels.cu:matmul_fp8_fused()+0x1a3

Tensor dump right before NaN (printed with .cpu().detach().numpy() for small slices):
- after attention matmul (shape [1, 16, 2048, 64]): sample float32 conversion of 8 values:
  [1.243e-02, 3.212e-03, 7.11e-05, -2.244e-04, 0.0, nan, nan, nan]
- corresponding quantized buffer (uint8 view): [0, 3, 12, 245, 128, 255, 255, 255] (note: 255 appears where float->fp8 mapping overflowed)

Repro notes: 
- With the same seed, fp8 run sometimes passes and sometimes fails — indicates non-determinism likely tied to kernel scheduling, mem reuse, or non-atomic ops.
- INT8 conversion path uses different matmul kernel (cublas-based) and does not show NaN.
- When I force paths to use cublas (disable fused kernels), fp8 run still fails in a couple of runs but less frequently.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) FP8 representation overflow/underflow + denormal handling causing write of special bit pattern that our kernel interprets as NaN on dequantization. (high prior)
2) A bug in fused matmul kernel when using post-scale + group-rounding: ordering of rounding vs clamping wrong -> produces 0xFF sentinel values. (medium)
3) Race condition in KV cache allocation/aliasing leading to stale memory being read as NaN (observed some pointer reuse patterns). (medium-low)
4) Compiler/vectorization incorrectly optimizing small path for a particular sm version (observed only on sm_80). (low)
5) Upstream libcudnn or driver bug with denormals interplay (less likely because BF16 unaffected). (low)

Quick evidence for hypothesis 1:
- Dumped raw bytes of quant buffer and saw 0xFF at places where float32 showed NaN. 0xFF is the encode for saturate/overflow sentinel in our fp8 scheme. 
- Running with CUDA_FLUSH_DENORMS_TO_ZERO=1 reduces frequency of NaN by ~60% in logs from last night.

Experiments done and results: (short log)
- disable-fused-gemm + seed 42 x 10 runs -> 2/10 NaN (was 7/10 initially)
- export CUDA_FLUSH_DENORMS_TO_ZERO=1 + fused kernels on -> 3/10 NaN
- force float32 interim accumulators (set env DEBUG_FORCE_ACC_FP32=1) -> 0/10 NaN (temp mitigation)
- run under nsight systems (brief) -> saw several kernels preempted, re-launched (scheduling churn)

Local patch tested: swapped rounding order (round->clamp -> store) to (clamp -> round -> store) in fp8 encode kernel. Compiled and smoke tested: reduced NaN frequency in single-run smoke but not deterministic. Opening PR for discussion: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2876 (WIP)

Next steps / triage plan:
- (A) Capture full GPU memory snapshot at failure and save quantized buffer (raw bytes) with offsets. Add instrumentation to kernel to log index where 0xFF appears.
- (B) Run with CUDA memcheck / compute-sanitizer to see illegal memory accesses (costly). Use small seq=128 to make it faster.
- (C) Re-run on different SM family (V100 if available) to confirm hardware-specific behavior.
- (D) Add checks in encode/decode paths to assert no 0xFF before dequant on CI-only debug build; if asserted, dump backtrace and full buffer.
- (E) Coordinate with compiler team to run with different nvcc flags (no fast-math, no fma) to detect math reorder sensitivity.

Data capture checklist (what to save on next fail):
- /tmp/fail-YYYYMMDD.fp8.raw (raw quant buffer)
- /tmp/fail-YYYYMMDD.tensor-slices.txt (few tensor slices around write)
- nvprof / nsight timeline snippet (10s around failure)
- runtime log with NVTX markers inserted around encode/decode + matmul

Immediate TODOs (short-term):
- [ ] Push temporary ASSERT in fp8_decode to catch 0xFF and log index (today)
- [ ] Add deterministic allocator option to avoid aliasing (next run)
- [ ] Schedule 2-hour run on V100/GPU-s with dev infra (tomorrow)
- [ ] Ping compiler folks with brief and ask for a quick repro compile (no-fast-math) (tomorrow)

Notes to future self / handoff:
- This one looks like an interaction between quantization sentinel values and kernel arithmetic ordering. If you see 0xFF in quant buffer repeatedly, prioritize code path that clamps earlier.
- If assertion fires only on high seq lengths, kv-cache growth may exacerbate memory aliasing — capture allocator logs.
- Slack thread: #quant-investigations (see pinned message from 2024-03-12)

Reference commands I used to dump raw bytes: (helpful)
python - <<'PY'
import numpy as np
buf = open('/dev/shm/quantbuf.bin','rb').read()
print(list(buf[:64]))
PY

End of session notes (2024-03-15 01:02):
- Filed Linear ticket QUANT-412 with basic repro + raw logs. Assigned to Asha for kernel review and Michael to coordinate CI assert.
- Will try temporary mitigation: force fp32 accumulators for production-critical queues until root cause fixed (costly but safe).

Misc scratch:
- could attempt to run golden-run diff: run bf16 and fp8 side-by-side and compute token-level divergence distance; capture at first divergence point and dump all intermediate activations (heavy but precise).

-- Riley
